title: Announcement bar shipping messaging is inconsistent and static
issue: The announcement bar says "Free U.S. Shipping $49+ / International $99+", but product pages show an icon with text that says "Fast & Free Shipping". This misleads customers because they don't actually get free shipping unless they meet a minimum order threshold. The bar also shows only one static message.
why_it_matters: Inconsistent shipping claims mislead customers and add friction; a rotating bar lets the site highlight several offers instead of just one.
recommendations: Clean up the shipping terminology so the announcement bar and product-page shipping messaging are consistent
Incorporate a free shipping threshold progress bar in the cart drawer

Implement a rotating announcement bar that cycles messages every ~5 seconds, e.g. free shipping thresholds, "100% Money Back Guarantee! Shop Now", a sale countdown, "Find the product that's right for you! Take the quiz", "X,XXX+ 5-Star Reviews from Happy Customers!", "Subscribe + Save Up to 50% OFF", or a first-order discount code (see HUM Nutrition and Salt.XO)

title: No site search in navigation and GA search tracking is off
issue: There is no search icon in the navigation, and Google Analytics' section for tracking search has not been turned on, so no onsite-search data is being captured.
why_it_matters: Visitors who use onsite search have more buyer intent — they are 1.8x more likely to convert, and onsite search can generate 13.8%-40% of a store's overall revenue. Search queries also let the store "listen" to customers passively (e.g. 100 searches per day for "gummies" would suggest offering a gummy variation).
recommendations: Add a search icon to the main navigation bar on desktop and inside the hamburger menu on mobile
Implement predictive search results that pre-populate when someone starts a search query
Turn on Search Tracking in Google Analytics

title: Text-only logo, no differentiated branded logo
issue: The site's "logo" is just a string of text rather than a unique, professional, differentiated logo. The audit marks this as a non-priority change.
why_it_matters: No matter the line of business, a unique and professional logo is needed to become a successful brand; text-based is not detrimental but adds no brand variety.
recommendations: Create a more differentiated logo in the future, even if it's just a more playful font

title: No ingredients/learning page despite frequent ingredient questions
issue: Customer inquiries frequently ask about the products, their ingredients, whether they're FDA approved, and if they're safe for pregnancy, but there is no dedicated ingredients/education page — ingredients exist only as a small string of text in the product description dropdown.
why_it_matters: It's common practice in the women's health/beauty supplements industry to create a separate ingredients page because customers really care about it; showing "we DO think about ingredients" lets customers focus on which product to purchase rather than whether the products are health-conscious and safe to use. A dedicated page also improves transparency, builds trust, declutters product pages, and enhances SEO.
recommendations: Add a navigation button that opens a dedicated ingredients/learning page
Make the first version broad — high-level info about the products being natural, having no dyes or parabens, etc. — and deepen it by product category later if it proves helpful
Include certifications/FDA approval info where available, plus FAQs addressing the key questions customers ask
Model it on HUM Nutrition's "clean + clinically tested" page, Vagisil, and FLO

title: No mega menu or benefit-based filtering in navigation
issue: The navigation has no filtering layers, so customers must click through the collection page to comprehend the different product types (Vag Odor, Vag Dryness, Dark Spots, etc.), adding unnecessary clicks on the way down the purchase funnel.
why_it_matters: Statistically, the fewer clicks a customer takes to get the information they're looking for, the quicker they'll convert and the less friction they'll experience.
recommendations: Build a mega menu that encapsulates all products, on both mobile and desktop (see OPositive, HUM, and Love Wellness)

Break the "Products"/"Shop" category into the benefits someone would be seeking: Vag Dryness, Vag Odor, Dark Spots, Ingrown Hairs, Body Odor, Vag Taste (e.g. Vag Dryness → Renew Oil, Slippery Pills; Body Odor → Body Magic Pills, Yummy Wash)
Still include a "Shop All" / "View All Products" button that takes people to the full collection page

Consider one of four restructuring options: (1) Shop button with high-level benefit filtering, (2) layered mega menu with products categorized by benefit, (3) "Shop By Benefit" separate from a main "Shop All", or (4) the live site's layout with more buttons — all including Ingredients, Our Story, Contact (Contact Us, FAQ), Take The Quiz, plus search and cart icons

title: Navigation bar is not sticky
issue: The navigation bar does not stick while scrolling — someone halfway down the home page can only reach a product page by scrolling several times back up the page.
why_it_matters: Requiring customers to scroll up and down a webpage to reach navigation is cumbersome and could lead to them leaving the website altogether because of the inaccessibility of navigation components.
recommendations: Keep the navigation sticky at all times (like HUM Nutrition), or
Make the navigation bar disappear when scrolling downward and reappear when the customer scrolls upward (like Cora)

title: Default navigation layout needs restructuring on mobile and desktop
issue: The default navigation view is laid out suboptimally: the logo and navigation buttons are in the wrong order (logo is not on the left), and the space between the logo and the right-hand icons is unused.
recommendations: On both mobile and desktop, put the logo on the left-hand side, navigation buttons after it, and the search icon/cart button on the far right
Test moving the mobile hamburger menu icon to the right-hand side of the page
Optionally add a "Take Quiz" or "Shop" CTA between the logo and the right-hand icons for quick access to the Shop All collection page
Add a search icon to the main layer of navigation

title: Featured products scroller assumes product knowledge visitors don't have
issue: The mobile home page shows a featured products scroller at the top, but visitors with little or no context click into it blindly — e.g. someone wanting help with Dark Spots might click "Body Magic" with no way to learn the benefits first. Heat mapping and screen recordings show the #1 clicked region is the below-the-fold "Which One" benefits section, and the navigation bar is another top-clicked region.
why_it_matters: Customers are looking for benefits-driven direction when they arrive rather than being told to check out a bundle; the top-clicked element being below the fold means the above-fold elements aren't providing the utility and direction visitors want.
recommendations: Alter the featured products scroller into a featured benefits scroller (showcase benefits rather than products people don't identify with yet)
Include more filtering capabilities throughout the navigation
Make the hero section less narrow in its approach of just sending people to the bundles page

title: Hero copy is vague and CTAs give no direction
issue: The hero uses blank statements like "Don't worry. It's safe here", "These Products Will Help", and "I had it before too…" that make no sense to a new visitor and don't explain the kinds of products sold. The hero CTA provides so little utility that visitors resort to the navigation bar instead.
why_it_matters: The hero needs to say what is being sold, the problem solved, how the brand is different, and where to go next; more direct copy lets customers comprehend the product offering coherently.
recommendations: Rewrite the hero copy to broadly explain the offering, e.g. "We're dedicated to restoring women's confidence with natural feminine products that are free of harsh chemicals and fillers"
Add an accent message above the headline such as "⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 40,000+ Reviews"
Test headline options like "Say Goodbye to Itching, Fishy Odor, and Irritation!", "Proven Solutions For Women's Feminine Wellness", or "Natural Solutions For Natural Problems"
Use two CTAs: primary "Shop All Products" plus a secondary "Bundle & Save" or "Need Help Choosing? Take Quiz →"
A/B test other CTA variations: Take The Quiz, See Ingredients, Subscribe & Get X% OFF

title: No model or lifestyle imagery anywhere on the website
issue: There is not a single image of a woman on the website — every image, including the hero, is graphic-based with no lifestyle or model imagery. The couple of testimonial videos that exist are displayed in a way that renders them obsolete. As a result the website looks like a graphic-designed website for a dropshipping company, not a brand.
why_it_matters: Model and lifestyle imagery makes customers feel more "at home" and like they "belong" to the community being sold to; every prominent competitor and major beauty-supplement brand uses model-based imagery, so its absence is a major red flag for best practices.
recommendations: Incorporate women throughout as many places on the website as possible — the home page hero section, the product pages, and anywhere else feasible

Test hero options: an image of a confident/happy woman or group of women (optionally combined with products), a shop-by-benefit hero using model imagery, lifestyle product photos instead of graphics, or a background video/GIF showcasing products and the primary customer (like Omnilux and Goli, with CTA buttons overlapping the video)
Invest in non-graphic "Lifestyle Content" across the site, accepting it requires an investment of time and money

title: Grammar error in hero subtext
issue: The last sentence of the home page hero subtext has a grammar error: "Luckily i figured out how to fix it for you" needs a capital "I".
why_it_matters: Small flaws in professionalism go a long way to deter customers from buying; when little issues like this happen, they add up negatively over time.
recommendations: Capitalize the "I" in the final sentence of the hero subtext

title: No press/news features below the hero section
issue: The home page has no news/press features beneath the hero section, which is common practice in the industry.
why_it_matters: News features under the hero add credibility and social proof at the moment visitors arrive.
recommendations: Either fabricate to some extent or get renowned blogs/news organizations to post about the brand
Place the features directly under the hero image like OPositive, with larger scroll arrows and auto-scrolling logos that require no customer action

title: No value propositions/USP section on the home page
issue: The home page lacks a value propositions section — there are no verbal/visual components highlighting differentiators or reasons the brand is good to buy from.
why_it_matters: Mentioning things like "natural products" and "free of harsh chemicals" primes customers to focus on product benefits rather than whether the ingredients are safe, and separates the brand from the crowd of other similar brands.
recommendations: Add a value propositions/USP section below the hero as a segue into the featured products section (see HUM and ELIX)
If product-centric propositions run short, use purchase-centric highlights: free shipping thresholds, return policies/guarantees, financing availability, and subscription/bundle savings

title: "What's Going On?" benefit filter buttons don't feature products
issue: The home page's "What's Going On?" filter buttons have two flaws: (1) clicking any benefit filter takes you to only one product even though multiple products address that benefit (the Vag Odor filter goes directly to a bundle), and (2) no actual products are featured in the section itself.
why_it_matters: Visitors click blindly into a benefit filter and may never learn other products address their symptom; it's hard for customers to understand the value a bundle provides without understanding all that is sold and each product's benefit.
recommendations: Add a products scroller below the filters that renders the products for the selected benefit (clicking "Vag Odor" shows odor products, "Vag Taste" shows taste products, etc.)
Add filters for Best Sellers, Bundles, and Shop All Products, similar to Love Wellness
Alternatively, redirect each benefit filter to the collection page showing the actual products that provide that benefit (like Love Wellness and SaltXO), ideally with lifestyle content
Future option: track browsing behavior and populate this section with previously viewed products ("pick up where you left off"), like Retrospec

title: No product-recommendation quiz
issue: The website has no quiz element, even though much of the competition and other beauty-based businesses leverage one.
why_it_matters: A quiz provides a more personalized experience that surfaces a relevant product, and simultaneously increases email capture (lead gen) by requesting an email at the end of the quiz to get results — fueling email marketing.
recommendations: Add a quiz element below the featured collections/products section on the home page (see Love Wellness and Honey Pot quizzes)
Showcase the quiz as a general navigation button as well
Consider a discount incentive: "Take the Quiz and get XX% OFF", so customers get a tailored recommendation plus a discount while the store captures their email even if they don't convert right away

title: No About Us section on the home page
issue: The home page has no About Us section, and the existing website seems more like a dropshipping brand a customer may or may not actually receive a product from — there is no founder, team, or story emphasis anywhere prominent.
why_it_matters: Beauty brands that aren't top-level names everyone knows build credibility by featuring the founders, team, or medical team behind the brand; an About Us section adds personality, depth, and credibility.
recommendations: Add a longer-form About Us section on the home page with an image (founders or team) and text — a personable video is even better; if against showing real images, use a lifestyle-like placeholder
Add a CTA to the section that takes customers to the About Us page, but only once that page is built out further
Follow ELIX's more personable layout approach

title: Home page reviews section is dull and unbelievable
issue: The reviews section on the home page feels dull — the reviews might be real, but the display isn't "decorated" or "believable", and it shows in-depth single-product reviews for products a visitor might have no context about yet.
why_it_matters: The most important thing to accomplish with reviews is for the customer to believe and know that what they're reading is real; otherwise the section is just wasting space.
recommendations: Redesign the section with personalization or real imagery of customers (see OPositive, Semaine, Salt.XO, and HUM)
Highlight a few broad reviews about the company/products in a nice-looking way rather than showing reviews for all products
Consider segmenting reviews by source (FB, Google, etc.) like Wing Bikes, if reviews exist on those platforms
Consider using third-party review platforms people know about to help with credibility
Get creative with the existing testimonial video buttons from the product pages and add them to the home page like Love Wellness

title: Customer service block and FAQs are disconnected
issue: The home page has a "Customer Service" block at the bottom and separately, recently-added FAQ dropdowns; the two sections are not combined, and FAQs provide more utility on the product page anyway.
why_it_matters: Visitors need one clear way to find information — FAQs, contact options, and more.
recommendations: Combine the customer service block with the FAQ dropdowns into one hybrid section
Include CTAs that direct people to (1) live chat or "Contact Us", (2) FAQs accessible without switching pages, and (3) the full FAQ page for in-depth information
Repurpose the FAQs for the product pages where they provide more utility

title: Active social media presence isn't showcased on the site
issue: Despite being active on social media with a nice following, the website has no Instagram feed/social account highlight.
why_it_matters: Seeing posting activity and professional-looking content makes visitors believe the brand is larger and more credible than they might have initially thought; it adds social proof, fresh content, SEO benefit, and engagement — anything that builds more trust helps conversions.
recommendations: Add an app like Instafeed (or something similar) to the bottom of the website
Feature the feed in strategic places — home page, product pages, and other value-driving pages — without taking away from the user experience

title: No subscribe-for-discount CTA near the footer
issue: The site has no subscribe option where a customer submits their email in exchange for a discount.
recommendations: Add a Subscribe CTA block either directly above the footer or within the footer itself, offering a discount in exchange for the customer's email

title: Footer has no shopping links
issue: The footer does not have anything pertaining to shopping — no way to get from the footer to the products collection page.
recommendations: At the very least, add a "Shop All Products" button to the footer
Revise the footer to mimic the changes recommended for the global navigation

title: No breadcrumbs on collection or sub-pages
issue: There are no breadcrumbs on the collection pages or any sub-pages, so visitors — especially those arriving from paid ads onto a collection page — don't know where they are in the grand scheme of the website.
why_it_matters: Breadcrumbs on all sub-pages are best practice; a simple "Home → All Products" trail helps customers understand where they are and where they can go.
recommendations: Add breadcrumbs (e.g. "Home → All Products") to collection pages and as many other sub-pages as possible

title: No review stars on collection page product listings
issue: Product listings on the collection page show no review stars — some products have 100s of reviews, but that isn't visible until the customer reaches the product page.
why_it_matters: Reviews related to a product are much more "moving" for a customer throughout their purchasing journey and provide credibility around the products.
recommendations: Add review stars and the actual review count to product listings on all pages where products are listed
Optionally add color to the review stars (like yellow), though just having stars will go a long way

title: Product listings lack containment and pricing wraps to two lines
issue: Product listings on the collection page feel "noisy" and disconnected because there is no container around the product image, title, pricing, and review stars. Additionally, the pricing font is so large that "USD" pushes onto the line below.
why_it_matters: Containers let customers more easily differentiate each product and its specific details; preventing pricing from taking two lines is required for the website to be mobile optimized.
recommendations: Add a container around each product listing (image, title, pricing, review stars) like HUM Nutrition and Love Wellness
Reduce the pricing font size so "USD" does not wrap onto a second line

title: No Add To Cart CTAs on collection page listings
issue: Product listings on the collection page have no CTAs — customers must click into the product page to add an item to cart.
why_it_matters: A customer who already evaluated a product (e.g. Renew Oil) and returns to the collection page should be able to purchase directly from the collection level instead of re-entering the product page.
recommendations: Add an Add To Cart button to product listings at the collection page level, like HUM Nutrition and OPositive
If the listing containers get too convoluted, show the Add To Cart button on hover instead of by default

title: Product short descriptions don't match the benefit-filter language
issue: The short descriptions below product titles on the collection page (e.g. "10X Vaginal Moisture" for Slippery Box) don't use the same benefit-filter language used elsewhere on the site.
why_it_matters: Making the short description match the benefit filters ("Vag Dryness" for Slippery Box, "Body Odor" for Yummy Wash) creates consistency and visual cues that teach customers to navigate by benefit — especially useful as more products are added in the future.
recommendations: Optionally make each product's short description exactly the same as its benefit filter
Note the future dilemma of a single product also fitting several benefit filter categories

title: Listings show only one-time price; subscribe & save price not surfaced
issue: Collection page listings show only the one-time purchase price even though the store has tiered subscription discounting.
why_it_matters: The subscription price is much lower than one-time and featuring it will likely reduce the bounce rate from the collection pages.
recommendations: Option 1: show both the one-time price AND the subscribe-and-save price in the listing container like Love Wellness, featuring the highest discount (the 1-month subscription option)
Option 2: keep showing the one-time price but clean up the font size so it doesn't run onto two lines

title: Price tags overlaid on product images provide no context
issue: Some product listings overlay the plain price on the product image. A price tag only stands out if there is a strikethrough price beside it, so this overlay is ineffective — customers can't understand the value of the listed price.
why_it_matters: Without a discount or compare-at price for context, the overlaid price communicates nothing of value.
recommendations: Replace the price overlay with the discount % OFF, or show the original price with a strikethrough (already done correctly on The Balance Bundle)

Alternatively use the overlay tags for other information like "Bundle & Save", "New Product", or the brand filter categories — though categories may get convoluted for products like Renew Oil that are part of multiple categories

title: No CTA blocks between product listings
issue: The collection page real estate between and around product listings is unused — there are no CTA blocks like "Take The Quiz" or "Subscribe & Save" that competing brands include.
why_it_matters: These CTAs aid in retention, increase the chances of conversions, and help with customer comprehension of the website overall.
recommendations: Incorporate CTA blocks in between and around the product listings (like RAD Bikes' and HUM's quiz action blocks)
Use helpful info as placeholders, e.g. "14-Day Money Back Guarantee on All Purchases" or "Free Shipping on Orders over $49 for USA orders"
In the future, use the blocks for discount codes or free-gift-with-purchase messaging

title: No benefit filters at the top of the collection page
issue: The collection page has no filtering to help customers quickly differentiate the products — there are no benefit filters at the top of the page.
why_it_matters: Benefit filters reduce the friction customers experience getting further down the funnel into product pages; with only a handful of products this is very effective.
recommendations: Add benefit filters to the top of the collection page so that clicking e.g. "Vag Odor" populates only the product(s) for Vag Odor (see Beam, HoneyPot, Vagisil, Love Wellness, SaltXO)
Consider including "All Products" (and possibly "Bundles") segments like Love Wellness
Decide whether filters also apply to the Bundles collection — filtering could just show the bundles related to the selected benefit

title: PDP testimonial videos are for the wrong products and lack context
issue: The video testimonial slider at the top of every product page shows testimonials for other products — e.g. viewing "REFRESH" still surfaces testimonials about "SLIPPERY BOX". Some videos never state which product they're about (in Testimonial #3 the customer just says a bunch of adjectives related to "wetness" without naming the product or the benefit).
why_it_matters: This is incredibly confusing to a site visitor and adds a lot of unnecessary friction to the buyer journey; it's likely why few people click this component compared to the product image gallery.
recommendations: Make every testimonial video on a product page explicitly related to that product — stating the product name and "helped me with {what it helps with}"
Shoot testimonials that cover the customer's problem, the product, and the benefit it provides, like BEAM's example
As a future test, consider a persistent hover-button testimonial widget in the bottom-left of the page

title: Product image galleries are thin on content
issue: Hotjar shows the image gallery thumbnails are the #1 clicked section within the entire product page, yet the galleries give customers little worth seeing. Google Analytics shows the lowest-converting product is Body Magic, which has only 3 pictures — a relatively minimal amount of imagery.
why_it_matters: Customers want to review images but aren't given content that incentivizes them to purchase; the less content on a product page, the worse the conversion outcome.
recommendations: Expand every product's image gallery with more and better content (lifestyle imagery, ingredients labels, benefit graphics, video)
Prioritize the lowest-content products like Body Magic

title: Social media comment screenshots dominate the image galleries
issue: A large portion of the gallery content is screenshots of social media comments; on some product pages they take up the majority of the image thumbnail real estate.
why_it_matters: A visitor's attention span is very small and it's unlikely customers will read images that require reading several sentences/paragraphs — they want quick, easy-to-digest imagery describing the product and its benefit.
recommendations: Keep social media comment images only as a supplementary bit of content, not the majority of thumbnails
Replace with more lifestyle-like content that evokes emotion, rather than only static colored, solid backgrounds

title: Attempted lifestyle imagery looks like an Alibaba listing
issue: The one attempt at lifestyle-oriented imagery in the galleries looks like an Alibaba listing or a factory photo — it doesn't feel branded and doesn't make anyone want to purchase. There is essentially no branded content featuring the primary customer on the website.
why_it_matters: Imagery needs to convey the branding; model-based content showing the target customer will definitely help with performance.
recommendations: Use images that showcase women living happier, symptom-free lives, or at the very least imagery featuring a woman
Model the lifestyle content on Semaine, Cora, and OPositive, which feels "REAL", "Professional", and "Branded"

title: Ingredient/supplement-facts imagery missing from galleries
issue: Supplement facts are not included in the product image galleries. Ingredients only appear as a small string of text in the product description dropdown, which is very unnoticeable and ineffective.
why_it_matters: One of the main questions customers ask when purchasing from supplement companies is about ingredients and whether the product is safe to use, and customers click gallery thumbnails very often — so the label needs to be where they look.
recommendations: Add ingredients label imagery to each product's image gallery
For bundles, add all component products' ingredient labels, similar to what OPositive does
Consider a bolded label below the product title that opens a nutrition-facts popup like BEAM (secondary to gallery placement)

title: Graphic-based images used without informative overlays
issue: Graphic-based images are used as the sole content to incentivize purchase on most product pages, without overlaying useful information a customer would want to know before buying (only some pages, like The Balance Bundle, do this).
why_it_matters: Graphics only add depth when they also convey product benefits or useful information.
recommendations: Include graphic-based images only when overlaying useful product information (benefits etc.), like Love Wellness does
Extend the overlay approach already used on The Balance Bundle to all other product pages

title: No video content in product galleries
issue: The product image galleries contain no videos.
why_it_matters: A brand looks and feels more credible when it has invested in video content — it signals a safe brand to buy from with real people operating the business.
recommendations: Make videos of no more than 30 seconds for each product
Options: a fun animated video about the product, customer testimonials, and/or a doctor/team member discussing the product benefits in more depth — or a combination (see HUM Nutrition's example)

title: Review stars missing from the product action block
issue: Review stars are not placed at or around the product title and price in the product action block, even though the products actually have dozens of reviews to showcase. Currently the only way to reach reviews is scrolling all the way down the page.
why_it_matters: Reviews are a major component of any product page — not emphasizing review stars near the title is a huge red flag. Stars there also make for a quick clickable segue down the page to the reviews.
recommendations: Move the review stars directly above or below the product title and product price component
Make the stars clickable so they jump to the reviews section

title: Quantity selector takes up prime buy-box real estate
issue: The quantity selector occupies prime real estate in the product action block, layering more choices on top of different pricing, purchase options, and delivery intervals.
why_it_matters: Seeing layers of different pricing, quantities, and delivery intervals can confuse the customer; removing the selector keeps the focus on the one-time vs subscription choice and makes the product CTA block shorter, which is nice for CRO purposes.
recommendations: Remove the quantity selector from the product page
Let customers increase quantity from within the cart/cart drawer after something gets added to cart

title: Static product price doesn't update with the subscription selector
issue: The static price stays fixed regardless of the selected purchase option — The Balance Bundle shows "$159 USD" below the title even when the "Subscribe & Save" option showing a different price is selected.
why_it_matters: Customers get confused when different prices show up in certain places; removing the static price shortens the page, makes it more usable, and reduces the friction surrounding pricing confusion — no surprises further down the funnel.
recommendations: Remove the price shown below the product title and let the one-time/subscription purchase selector carry the pricing
Dynamically change the Add To Cart button label to include the selected price, e.g. "Add To Cart - $159"

title: "Buy with Google" and "More Payment Options" clutter the buy box
issue: The buy box includes a "Buy with Google" button and a "More Payment Options" button in addition to Add To Cart — on top of the one-time, 1-month, 2-month, and 3-month purchase option variants, it ends up being 5+ buttons.
why_it_matters: The experience is more convoluted than it needs to be; in several past client tests, removing the "More Purchase Options" component led to a better user experience and an increase in website performance, and it's often hard to find brands that leave these options in.
recommendations: Remove "Buy with Google" and the "More Payment Options" button, keeping one primary Add To Cart CTA
Test the removal to see if there is a net benefit

title: Long-form description overwhelms; Read More can't be collapsed
issue: The product description is a long-form block that expects the customer to read everything like a book to find the small detail they actually care about. There is also a functional flaw: clicking "Read More" expands the section with no way to minimize it, making it very cumbersome to scroll the page to view images and pricing option blocks.
why_it_matters: Breaking information into targeted accordion dropdowns lets customers click directly into the info they care about most, which will help get more conversions.
recommendations: Keep only an abbreviated short description — a sentence or two explaining what the product is and how it can benefit a customer
Fix or remove the un-collapsible "Read More" behavior

Replace the long-form description with accordion dropdowns: "Why You'll Love It" (benefits like removing dark marks, bumps, and odor), "Recommended Usage" (amount per day/use/serving in a skimmable design like OPositive and Omnilux), and "Ingredients" (presented aesthetically with the nutrition label, not just subtle text)
Optionally add an FAQ accordion or a "Have Questions? Chat With Us →" button beneath the accordions linking to the live chat widget

title: Pricing options and ATC button sit too far from the product title
issue: The pricing option blocks sit low in the product action block instead of close to the product title (a gap made worse once the static price label is removed per the audit's other recommendation).
why_it_matters: Pricing info should be as close to the product title as possible.
recommendations: Move the pricing option blocks and Add To Cart button up to directly below the short description section, like Love Wellness and De Lune

title: Value props misplaced, secure badges excessive, shipping claim inaccurate
issue: The value propositions (Fast & Free Shipping, Secure Payments, 14-Day Risk Free Purchase) are not below the Add To Cart button; excess secure-checkout badges sit below the ATC button; and the "Fast & Free Shipping" value proposition is inaccurate because there is actually a $49 USD free shipping threshold.
why_it_matters: Value props directly beneath the ATC button push customers further down the funnel; inaccurate claims mislead customers.
recommendations: Relocate the Fast & Free Shipping, Secure Payments, and 14-Day Risk Free Purchase value propositions to below the Add To Cart button
Add "Cancel Anytime" as a value proposition; on mobile, swap out Secure Payments for Cancel Anytime if only 3 fit the design
Replace the Free Shipping value proposition with something else if it's inaccurate given the $49 threshold
Remove the excess value propositions/secure checkout badges currently below the Add To Cart button
Consider text-based value proposition messages beneath the ATC button like many other companies use

title: Product page is empty below the buy box despite 95% scroll depth
issue: Below the product action block the page goes straight into the reviews section — there is not enough branded content and the page feels very empty and unfinished. Screen recording data shows 95% of people made it below the fold, so added content would likely be received well.
why_it_matters: Customers are probably anticipating content there in the first place; every prominent beauty-supplement brand has additional content lower down the page going over ingredients, features, reviews, and much more.
recommendations: Add a benefits section with logos/icons plus text offering product-based value propositions (like Omnilux LED, Beam, and Love Wellness), ideally with lifestyle or more playful/branded imagery
Add a mid-page FAQ section repurposing the home page FAQs — covering shipping, safety, etc. (see De Lune, Femiclear, Love Wellness) — if the FAQ isn't placed in the description accordions

Add a "Frequently Bought With" or "You May Also Like" section below or directly above the review widget (like HUM Nutrition and BEAM); test single products vs bundles as the recommendations, and show only non-bundle products if upsell strategies are running elsewhere
Build the mid-page content around the accordion topics: ingredients, benefits, how to use

title: Static review element below the buy box looks forced and dull
issue: The section with static reviews from customers below the product action block looks forced, dull, and ineffective.
why_it_matters: This section needs to provide as much credibility as possible.
recommendations: Replace the static review with video testimonials — the same ones at the top of the product pages can be reused, granted they're specific to the product page being browsed
Alternatively use nice images with reviews that look more believable
If any celebrities or popular influencers use the product(s) and would be ok with it, showcase them as advocates

title: Loox reviews widget shows wrong-product reviews and looks fake
issue: The Loox review widget at the bottom of the product pages shows reviews for all products rather than only the product page a customer is browsing, and its layout looks tacky, hard to read, and below the standard of how most prominent ecommerce brands display reviews.
why_it_matters: Loox is abused a lot by brands faking reviews, so it ends up looking pretty fake; wrong-product reviews create the same confusion as the testimonial videos at the top of the page.
recommendations: Show only reviews for the product page the customer is browsing
Move to a review widget that looks more credible, like stamped.io-style layouts
Add review filters like the age range of the reviewer and reason for use, like Beam
Consider a "Questions" component where visitors ask questions and the company responds — it serves as an FAQ of sorts and makes the brand look active and legitimate
Keep an emphasis on review imagery

title: No free gift or add-on/cross-sell mechanics on product pages
issue: Product pages have no free-gift or add-on component to prime customers to purchase or to raise AOV.
why_it_matters: A gift increases the perception around the products and gets people more "primed" to make a purchase; cross-sells/up-sells on single-product pages help generate the conversion AND increase the AOV.
recommendations: Offer a complimentary gift — per data, say "Complementary" instead of "FREE" and show the gift's original value so people understand they're getting something special and not just a cheap trinket (see Mindful Souls and BEAM's first-time-subscription frother)
Consider a static gift applied to every purchase, or a minimum order amount to qualify (which also helps customers meet the free shipping threshold)

On single-product pages, list cross-sell/up-sell options below the Add To Cart button within the action block — either a complementary product or two, or the bundle the product is already part of (see OPositive, Femiclear, HoneyPot)
Do NOT incorporate upsell elements on bundle product pages — that's already the nature of a bundle; at most use the complimentary gift there
If both concepts are validated through data, test a hybrid free-gift + add-on section

title: Mobile PDP sub-navigation concept
issue: If the product page gets longer per the audit's recommendations, mobile users will have no quick way to jump to the key information on the PDP.
why_it_matters: A sub-navigation makes the key PDP information readily accessible by the click of a button, and its click data (heat maps/screen recordings) reveals what people actually care about, informing the PDP design direction.
recommendations: Implement a product-page sub-navigation structure similar to Fashionova and Vagisil
Use the resulting heat map and screen recording insight to guide future PDP design

title: No wishlist functionality
issue: The site has no wishlist functionality on product pages or product listings.
why_it_matters: Wishlists help with email lead gen and remarketing purposes.
recommendations: Add wishlist functionality either below the ATC button or as a heart icon overlaying the product photos

title: No sticky Add To Cart / Buy Now button
issue: The primary CTA is not always accessible while a prospective customer scrolls the product page.
why_it_matters: A sticky buy button keeps the primary CTA always accessible.
recommendations: Test a sticky Buy Now/ATC button appended to the top or bottom of the product page

When products require a one-time vs subscription selection, do NOT send to checkout unless an option was expressly selected — label the button "Choose Option" and anchor the customer back up the page to the selector
Only implement if it does not negatively counteract other optimization techniques added to the product pages

title: USD prices use a comma instead of a period as decimal separator
issue: USD purchase prices display with a comma as the decimal separator rather than a period — a bug in the currency formatting.
why_it_matters: This can definitely inhibit customers from purchasing when they're from the USA.
recommendations: Fix the currency formatting so USD uses a period instead of a comma (bug-fix recommendation)

title: Upsells fire as a forced pre-cart popup instead of living in the cart drawer
issue: The site's up-sell plugin currently shows a pre-cart pop-up with upsells, which feels a bit too forced and disconnected from the cart itself.
why_it_matters: Blending the up-sells into the cart/cart drawer itself (rather than keeping them separate) reduces friction and helps AOV.
recommendations: Blend up-sells and cross-sells into the cart/cart drawer itself

Promote either bundles or single products from within the cart drawer — e.g. if the "Refresh" Cleansing Gel is in the cart, offer the "Refresh - 3PK" bundle option plus another alternative complementary product, like OPositive does
Don't double up: if upsells run at the product-page level, don't also run the current upsell pop-up during checkout

title: No urgency element in the cart
issue: There is no urgency mechanic in the cart when customers are about to purchase.
why_it_matters: Leveraging urgency at the moment of purchase nudges customers to complete checkout.
recommendations: Add a cart countdown timer with copy like "We'll hold onto this product for you for 10 minutes… This product is almost out of stock", "This price is only available for another 10 minutes", or "Items will remain in your bag for 10 minutes"
Consider Amazon's less "salesy" alternative: a quicker-shipping incentive telling customers that if they purchase now, they'll receive the product quicker

title: No free gift with purchase in the cart/checkout flow
issue: The cart/checkout flow offers no free gift with purchase.
why_it_matters: A free gift incentivizes customers to complete their purchase and can raise AOV as customers add items or spend more to qualify; framing it as "complementary" avoids looking cheap the way a discount might (like Ulta handing out testers that cost virtually nothing but psychologically keep customers coming back).
recommendations: Offer a free/complimentary gift within the cart drawer or checkout flow — applied automatically to every purchase or unlocked when a threshold (like free shipping) is met

title: No free shipping threshold progress bar in the cart drawer
issue: Despite having free shipping thresholds ($49 US / $99 international), the cart drawer has no progress bar showing customers how close they are to qualifying.
why_it_matters: A progress bar encourages customers to add more items to their cart, increases average order value, reduces cart abandonment caused by unexpected shipping costs, and improves the user experience by clarifying how much more to spend for free shipping.
recommendations: Add a free shipping threshold progress bar to the cart drawer

title: Cart says "Calculated at checkout" even when free shipping is earned
issue: Even when the free shipping threshold is met, the cart still says shipping is "Calculated at checkout" at the bottom where the checkout button is displayed.
why_it_matters: This is misleading to customers who have already qualified for free shipping.
recommendations: Dynamically change the label to say "free shipping" when the threshold is met
If it's not possible to change in the code (which it should be), remove the line entirely rather than showing text that doesn't register to the customer's specific cart total/situation

title: Cart button label "Checkout" feels too forced
issue: The cart drawer button is labeled "Checkout", which feels a bit too forced — as if buying something without fully reviewing the order.
why_it_matters: A subtle labeling change that reassures customers they can still review their order before paying.
recommendations: Change the cart drawer button label from "Checkout" to "Proceed to Checkout"

title: Discount code field hidden behind "Show Order Summary" on mobile
issue: On the mobile checkout page, the discount code field is hidden within the "Show Order Summary" section, which customers often can't find.
why_it_matters: This kind of subtle adjustment has been seen to lift conversions by quite a bit — especially for stores where mobile traffic is the most prominent source of attention.
recommendations: Rename "Show order summary" to "Add Discount/Coupon Code" or "See Summary & Add Discounts" (applicable if a discount approach is adopted in the future)

title: No review stars on products shown in the cart
issue: Products displayed in the cart page/drawer have no review stars next to them.
why_it_matters: Even though a customer who added an item likely already trusts the product, review stars in the cart provide some nice reassurance at the moment of purchase.
recommendations: Show review stars alongside the product(s) in the cart page/drawer

title: Website has no favicon
issue: The website has no favicon — the browser tab looks noticeably dull compared to other tabs; while auditing with many tabs open, the auditor kept thinking the site's tab was not an active page.
why_it_matters: A favicon aids brand recognition, creates a more professional/polished appearance that builds trust, helps users quickly identify the tab among many, and improves brand consistency across touchpoints.
recommendations: Add a favicon featuring the brand logo or other brand elements

title: "Recently ordered" popup is spammy and fires every few seconds
issue: A "recently ordered" pop-up shows up roughly every 5 seconds during a session but only displays for 1-2 seconds — too fast to read — repeatedly pulling attention away from important information.
why_it_matters: It's annoying and "spammy", no one really takes this tactic seriously these days, and the unreadably short display time compounds the negative effects on the user experience.
recommendations: Remove the recently-ordered pop-up entirely
If keeping it, show it once every 1-2 minutes instead of every 5-10 seconds

title: No chat widget / chatbot automations
issue: The website does not use a chat widget at all.
why_it_matters: Chatbots capture visitor emails even from non-converting traffic (feeding email marketing audiences), create real-time conversations that surface friction analytics can't (pricing complaints, custom quantities, findability issues), and recurring questions can be added to the FAQs to help future customers.
recommendations: Add a chat widget with the goal of 90+% automation, with a personal touch every once in a while

Trigger promotions: first-visit incentive (15% OFF in exchange for email), return-visit reminder of the previous offer (15% OFF), abandoned-cart sequence asking about friction with up to 20% OFF if they haven't already been given a discount, and a post-purchase message (next-purchase discount, upsell, thank you)
Automate general customer service help, redirecting to FAQs, promoting the quiz, and linking people to Ingredients

title: Test Spin-to-Win popup against the current Mystery Prize popup
issue: The site already runs a "MYSTERY PRIZE"-styled email popup, but alternative, more interactive popup formats haven't been tested.
why_it_matters: A Random Deal Generator (Spin to Win) is more interactive and engaging than a simple submission form — even if a lower discount is always granted, being able to "promote" up to 30% off increases the amount of email submissions.
recommendations: A/B test a Spin-to-Win popup against the current Mystery Prize approach
If a chat widget is added, coordinate the two so they don't overlap negatively

title: About Us page is very lackluster
issue: The existing About Us page is very lackluster and needs improvement — it doesn't tell the brand's story or show the people behind the brand.
why_it_matters: An "our story"/"about us" page builds trust and credibility, helps customers connect with the brand on a deeper level and become loyal advocates, provides background on the founders and mission, highlights unique selling points (sourcing, manufacturing), and enhances SEO.
recommendations: Rebuild the About Us page with the brand's story, values, founders, and team
Model it on OPositive, Beam, and Love Wellness
